summary: Takashi Yamada is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who studied at Hosei University. He held a post as assistant professor at the Prefectural University of Kumamoto (attested 2003).
Takatoshi Ito is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He held posts as professor at Komazawa University, attested in 1981 and 1991.
Takatoshi Nakamura is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ryukai Mano in 1979. He held a research post at Taisho University's Institute for Comprehensive Studies of Buddhism (attested 1978).

Takayasu Higuchi studied at Kyoto University (~1939–1942), working in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He served as professor at Kyoto University (~1967–1983) and director at Sen-oku Hakukokan Museum, Archaeological Institute of Kashihara, and Research Centre for Silk Roadology.

Takayasu Kimura, a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies, completed doctoral coursework at Taisho University. In 1995, he held posts as lecturer at Taisho University and researcher at the Institute of Modern Religious Education of Shingon Buzan.
Takayasu Suzuki is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1984–1993). Around 2008, he served as a professor at Yamaguchi Prefectural University.

Takayoshi Kamei was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1910–1913). He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1923–1947), Ibaraki University (~1949–1957), and Seisen University (~1957–1968).

Takayoshi Namikawa, an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar, completed his studies and doctorate at Bukkyo University. He was appointed professor there in 1981 and professor emeritus in 2018, also holding positions at Jawaharlal Nehru University and Hokkaido University.

Takayuki Hirosawa works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen and held positions at Taisho University, where he was a group member until 1991 and attested as professor in 2014.

Takehiro Sueki was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1942–1945). He held academic posts at the University of Electro-Communications (~1950–1957), the University of Tokyo (~1957–1982), and Toyo University (~1982–1992).

Takeo Hibino was a historian and Sinologist who studied at Kyoto University (~1933–1936). He worked at the Kyoto Institute of the Academy of Oriental Culture, Kyoto University (1948–1977), Otemon Gakuin University (1977), and Otemae University (1980) as professor and president.
Takeo Izumi is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tohoku University (~1974–1981) and later served as a professor there (~1996–2017).

Takeo Kanaseki, who studied at Kyoto University (~1919–1923), was a scholar in history and archaeology. He held posts at Kyushu University (~1950–1960), Tottori University (~1960–1967), and Tezukayama Gakuin University (~1967–1979).
Takeo Kuwabara studied at Kyoto University (~1925–1928). He held academic posts at Tohoku University (~1931–1943) and served as a professor at Kyoto University (~1948–1968).

Takeshi Fujii is a historian and Indologist who studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies and the University of Delhi. He spent his career at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, serving as assistant, lecturer, associate professor, professor, and professor emeritus (2021).

Takeshi Hasegawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. His academic posts include lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 1998), International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2026), and International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Takeshi Karashima was a Sinologist who studied at Tokyo Imperial University (~1923–1926). He held posts at Keijo Imperial University (~1928–1945), Sagami Women's University, Showa Women's University, and Kamakura's library.

Takeshi Umehara studied at Kyoto University under Tokuryu Yamauchi and Michitaro Tanaka. Active in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Japanology, he held posts at Ryukoku University, Ritsumeikan University, Kyoto City University of Arts, and directed the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (1987–1995).

Takeshiro Kuraishi was a scholar of Sinology and linguistics who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1918–1921). He served as professor at Kyoto University (~1939–1949), worked at the University of Tokyo (~1949–1958), and chaired the Society of Chinese Linguistics (~1968–1974).

Takezo Kaneko was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1925–1928) under Tetsuro Watsuji. He held posts at Hokkaido University (~1942–1947), the University of Tokyo (~1947–1965 as professor), International Christian University (~1965–1975), and Seikei University (~1975–1980).
